headline: COMED selectively escalates cross-model collaboration to trade rescue gains against collaboration harms
summary: The Sep. 22, 2026 COMED paper studies when a multi-model system should trust its initial answer, check it with a peer, or invoke fuller collaboration. The controller uses anchor self-consistency, router ambiguity and a lightweight peer probe to direct additional model calls toward uncertain or persistently disagreeing cases. In its reported benchmark suite, COMED improves its fixed or routed anchor in all 16 open-weight settings, averaging 4.6 percentage points while using at most two distinct models per query and about 33% fewer decoded tokens than dense collaboration. A Frontier-3/Humanity's Last Exam stress test reports GPT-5.5 rising from 23.13% to 28.13%, with collaboration on 70% of examples. These are paper-reported results; independent reproduction and implementation evidence remain open.
